definitions.explanation: The act of keeping watch over something, or the person assigned to keep watch. Used in both literal security contexts and more casual situations.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたちが{遊|あそ}ぶ{間|あいだ}、{見張|みは}り{役|やく}をしていた。
examples.english: I was on lookout duty while the children played.

examples.japanese: {倉庫|そうこ}の{前|まえ}に{見張|みは}りが{二人|ふたり}{配置|はいち}されていた。
examples.english: Two guards were stationed in front of the warehouse.

notes:
Derived from the verb {見張|みは}る (to keep watch). Can refer to either the act of watching or the person doing the watching.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見張|みは}りを{立|た}てる: to post a lookout
- {見張|みは}り{役|やく}: the role of lookout, the person on watch
- {見張|みは}り{台|だい}: watchtower, observation platform
- {見張|みは}り{番|ばん}: sentry, watchman
- {見張|みは}りをする: to keep watch

USAGE:
Appears in both serious contexts (military, security, crime stories) and everyday situations (watching children, keeping an eye on something cooking). In casual use, it often implies monitoring informally rather than formal guard duty.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {監視|かんし}: surveillance, monitoring (formal, systematic)
- {警備|けいび}: security, guard duty (professional)
- {番人|ばんにん}: guard, watchman (person)
